cat > /tmp/agents_m6.py <<'PYEOF'
MD = "/Users/dct/.factory/missions/e194b9e3-6a67-42b9-bfc9-dd4e1ac23b0c"
p = MD + "/AGENTS.md"
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()

sec = '''## M6 rules (inbox 1319; in force from the first M6 dispatch, 2026-10-30)

Owner, 30-oct, 13:19: "let's carry this work in M6" (inbox `2026-10-30-1319-m6-carries-the-validation-rules.md`; the long form is inbox 1350, rows 91 to 111 of contract-work/m4-boundary-questions.md). The record from M1 to M5: validation has cost 89 to 105 USD-eq per milestone while the build fell to about 61; in M5 validation cost one and a half times the build. Rules, as written:

1. "Contract readiness before the first dispatch, and the contract frozen for the unit: every assertion claimed by one slice and testable with its named tool; every owner input present or the assertion moved; integration-dependent assertions sequenced after integration; ambiguous wording rewritten before the build; no contract pass between dispatch and boundary."
2. "A claim is a receipt: a worker's hand-off lists each claimed assertion with the exact command it ran and its output; validators replay mechanical claims and spend judgement only on behavioural and mixed ones."
3. "From round 2, re-grade only the affected assertions, carrying the passed set as evidence."
4. "No dismissal of a hand-off item without the assertion grep; an item that names behaviour an assertion covers is a fix."
5. "Validators as leads with Sonnet seats (Rule D), and the owner will consider a cheaper model for the user-testing validator kind; scrutiny keeps judgement on Opus."
6. "Owner inputs named by the contract are readiness rows with a date and an inbox nag: the reference CSV, the owner screenshots."

- **Verdict condition.** "M6's verdict condition: validation under the build's cost." With inbox 1350 item 2: zero "as worded" failures and zero in-unit contract passes; a pass needed in flight is a boundary item with its cost.
- **Record per unit.** "validation share of cost and time, rounds and failed rounds, assertions re-tested per round, dismissed items later failed."
- **(a) The contract is frozen** from the carry-over dispatch (`m6-carryover-fix-pr-gate`) to the M6 boundary; pass 40 (2026-10-30 ~12:50Z) was the last pass. A failure "as worded" is a boundary item, not an in-flight pass. The freeze time is written in contract-work/m6-readiness.md.
- **(b) Claims are receipts.** Every claimed assertion in a hand-off lists the exact command run and its output under `### Claims (rule 30)`.
- **(c) No dismissal without the grep.** The orchestrator dismisses no hand-off item without first grepping validation-contract.md for the behaviour it names; a hit is a fix feature.
- **(d) Affected-only re-grading.** Validators re-grade only the affected assertions from round 2, carrying the passed set.
- **(e) Owner inputs are dated readiness rows** in contract-work/m6-readiness.md (reference CSV, owner screenshots, tauri-plugin-dialog decision), with a nag at the boundary before the unit that needs them.

'''
s = s.replace(marker, sec + marker)
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)

t = MD + "/library/tooling.md"
u = open(t, encoding="utf-8").read()
assert "inbox 1350" not in u
if not u.endswith("\n"): u += "\n"
u += '''
## Factory product asks and tool facts (M5 boundary, inbox 1350)

- Wake-rewrite class (item 4; add to Factory product feedback item 21). At four consecutive runner wakes (03:56, 04:12, 04:20, 04:29) the orchestrator wrote 162 k to 210 k tokens each (2.1 to 2.7 USD-eq, about 10 in 35 min) with cacheRead fixed at 38,164 every time, while the heartbeat turns between them read the cache. The usage report's Lead context rewrites table counts three by its strict rule (cache write minus read at least the context size, 157,521): 00:52Z, 03:20Z and 03:29Z, all three with cacheRead 38,164, 7.82 USD-eq in all. Detector: the same short cacheRead at successive wakes, not write minus read. Product ask: a stable prompt prefix across heartbeat and runner-wake turns, or a documented reason it differs. Candidates in the record: the compaction summary re-attached at 04:40 with numMessagesRemoved 1898; midConversationToolChangesActive true all day; the 01:52 occurrence predates the 04:40 re-attach.
- Model-Router (item 5; Factory product item 23). The router moved the orchestrator from claude-fable-5.1 to kimi-k3 at 04:43:46 (overage_proactive), a user-testing seat at 04:43:45 (overage_reactive_402), two self-check sessions at 04:48 and 04:50, and the Opus validator 364e8787 at 05:13:59. Seats check their model only at start: six seat sessions ran 54 turns on kimi-k3 between 04:43 and 05:11 before one noticed. The router did not restore the declared model after the window reset (confirmed 05:51); the owner restored it in the TUI at 06:27:48Z (07:27 local) and resumed at 07:38; mission held 2 h 53 min. Product asks: pause, do not route, by default, for the orchestrator and every subagent; tell the session at the moment its model changes; restore the declared model on reset; a model_changed event in the progress log. Owner, 07:32: "our bill is being impacted because of the limits setting, that is bad UX."
- Desktop client (item 14; Factory product item 22). The Factory desktop app, attached to the running session, cancelled the mission's calls at 21:04 on 29-oct ("Tool execution cancelled by user"; worker 53b27368 cut mid-edit with six files partial) and paused it again at 21:47 (a second client loaded the session). Cost: one 31-minute worker and 51 minutes of wall. Factory.app was quit at 21:50 and stays closed for any running mission; the observatory attaches read-only to the record and is the safe way to watch. Product asks: one driver per session, second clients read-only by default; the cancel names its client; a cancelled worker's partial edits are discarded or handed off with the file list.
- Gate tests never read host state (item 13). scripts/tests/usage_test.py read the host's boot time and the final gate went red after the host rebooted at 07:12:35 local; fixed by m5-fix-usage-test-boottime (pins --boottime; a test fails if a runner stops passing it; gate on code tree f0f20497 green at 11:01:40Z). A gate reads the tree and the record, never boot time, uptime, pids, ports or the clock.
'''
open(t, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(u)
